PullRequest.Title: customEditors: await the navigation request instead of polling in tests
PullRequest.Body:

Follow-up to #342698, which added `local/code-no-timeout-polling-loop` and listed `mainThreadCustomEditors.test.ts` in its `exclude` option. That PR has merged, so this one targets `main` directly.

## Problem

Two navigation tests in `src/vs/workbench/api/test/browser/mainThreadCustomEditors.test.ts` polled with `while (!x) { await timeout(0); }`:

- `navigation resolution is canceled when its panel closes before completion` (`while (!complete)`)
- `selection notifications during navigation resolution supersede its initial snapshot` (`while (!publish)`)

Both were waiting for the same thing: the fake extension host's `$resolveCustomTextEditorNavigation` being called, so the panel is disposed, or a selection is published, while navigation resolution is pending. The fake recorded that call indirectly by assigning `complete`/`publish` inside a `new Promise(resolve => ...)` executor. The loops did not wait on the call itself. They spun renderer timers, which are clamped to about 4 ms after a few nested ticks, until a later macrotask saw the side effect. The loops were unbounded, so they could not run out, but the time spent in them depended on timer clamping and machine load. They also needed `| undefined` locals and a `panelHandle!` non-null assertion.

## Change

The fake now completes a `DeferredPromise` with the token or panel handle when it is called, and the test awaits it. The extension host's reply is a second `DeferredPromise` that the test completes at the same point where it previously called `complete()`/`publish()`.

| Test | Waited for | Now awaits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `navigation resolution is canceled when its panel closes before completion` | `$resolveCustomTextEditorNavigation` called (polled `complete`) | `navigationRequested.p`, which resolves to the cancellation token passed to the extension host |
| `selection notifications during navigation resolution supersede its initial snapshot` | `$resolveCustomTextEditorNavigation` called (polled `publish`) | `navigationRequested.p`, which resolves to the panel handle |

Both scenarios are unchanged. `MainThreadCustomEditors.resolveCustomTextEditorNavigation` registers the pending selection, the dispose listeners and the cancellation source synchronously before calling the proxy, so resuming right after the call reaches the same state the loop did, one macrotask earlier. The test still disposes the panel or publishes the selection, then awaits the resolution and completes the reply in the same order, and every assertion is kept.

There are no product-code changes. `src/vs/workbench/api/test/browser/mainThreadCustomEditors.test.ts` is removed from the rule's `exclude` list in `eslint.config.js`. The `timeout` import stays because other tests in the file still use single `await timeout(0)` calls, which the rule does not report.

## Validation

- Baseline before the change, `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/api/test/browser/mainThreadCustomEditors.test.ts`: 15 passing (28 ms).
- Lint with the exclude list disabled, `npx eslint --rule '{"local/code-no-timeout-polling-loop": ["warn", {"exclude": []}]}' src/vs/workbench/api/test/browser/mainThreadCustomEditors.test.ts`: 2 warnings (292:4, 344:4) before, 0 problems after.
- 10 runs after the change, `for i in $(seq 10); do ./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/api/test/browser/mainThreadCustomEditors.test.ts 2>&1 | grep -E 'passing|failing'; done`: 10/10 with 15 passing (17-31 ms). Durations did not change notably.
- Under CPU load (18 `yes` processes), `lockf -t 3600 /tmp/vscode-no-timeout-polling-stress.lock bash -c 'pids=(); for i in $(seq 18); do yes > /dev/null & pids+=($!); done; ./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/api/test/browser/mainThreadCustomEditors.test.ts 2>&1 | grep -E "passing|failing"; kill "${pids[@]}"'`: 15 passing (33 ms). The original loops are unbounded, so they cannot run out under load, and I did not run the original version under load.
- Mutation checks, each applied temporarily and run with `--grep "navigation resolution"`, then restored byte-identically:
  - Cancellation test, reading `navigationRequested.value` instead of awaiting: fails with `undefined !== true` (the panel is disposed before navigation is requested).
  - Cancellation test, fake never completes `navigationRequested`: fails with a 5000 ms timeout.
  - Selection test, reading `navigationRequested.value!` instead of awaiting: fails with `undefined !== { ...selection }` (the selection is published before navigation is pending).
  - Selection test, fake never completes `navigationRequested`: fails with a 5000 ms timeout.
  - Product code, passing `CancellationToken.None` instead of `lifetime.token` to `$resolveCustomTextEditorNavigation`: the cancellation test fails on `isCancellationRequested`.
  - Product code, using `result.selection` instead of `pending.changed ? pending.selection : result.selection`: the selection test fails with `undefined !== { ...selection }`.
- `lockf -t 3600 /tmp/vscode-no-timeout-polling-typecheck.lock npm run typecheck-client`: no errors in the changed file. The run reported 60 errors, all in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/**/copilot*`, because the local `node_modules` has `@github/copilot-sdk` 1.0.20-preview.2 while `package.json` pins 1.0.23-preview.5. They are unrelated to this change.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/api/test/browser/mainThreadCustomEditors.test.ts eslint.config.js` (repo config with the updated exclude list): passed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cancellation navigation test waits until the in-process fake extension host receives the resolve request, then disposes the panel
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The test calls CustomEditorInput.resolve(), which synchronously reaches the in-process SingleProxyRPCProtocol fake after editor setup; navigationRequested completes at that call, disposal cancels raceCancellation, and the test resolution proceeds without waiting for the fake navigation reply. The changed await is on the test's critical path but replaces timer-driven macrotasks with one promise continuation.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A single navigation request in this test. Before the diff, timer turns scaled with scheduler delay until the request arrived; after the diff, one promise wake-up serves the request.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One input resolution and one fake navigation request are active. The cancellation race and fake reply promise overlap exactly as before; there is no queue, limiter, or aggregate concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates. Both cold and repeated test runs construct fresh fixtures and DeferredPromises; there are no keys, misses, negative states, or coalescing concerns.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the deleted loop scheduled timeout(0) repeatedly until the fake call assigned a callback, while the added DeferredPromise is completed by that same fake call and awaited once. The proxy and services are test doubles, so no real IPC, filesystem, database, network, or subprocess boundary is reached.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact CI savings vary with timer clamping and host load, but the change removes rather than adds repeated scheduling. Two DeferredPromise objects add only bounded per-test allocation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. The diff removes unbounded repeated timer scheduling and preserves bounded cleanup: disposal cancels the race, then the test completes the underlying fake reply.

Scenarios.Scenario: Selection-during-navigation test waits until the in-process fake receives the panel handle, publishes one selection, and completes resolution
Scenarios.CriticalPath: CustomEditorInput.resolve() reaches the fake navigation resolver; awaiting navigationRequested resumes immediately after that call, then one selection notification and one DeferredPromise completion allow resolution to finish. The direct signal replaces a polling loop on the test critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One panel and one selection notification. The old work scaled with elapsed scheduler turns; the new work remains constant.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One pending input resolution and one fake reply are active. Selection publication is serialized after request receipt and before reply completion; no burst or parallel fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is read or populated. Every run creates one fresh fixture and two fresh DeferredPromises, with no reusable or negative state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: call flow through SingleProxyRPCProtocol is in-process, and the added signal completes exactly once from resolveNavigation. No transitive subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation exists in the fixture path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The removed polling cost depended on scheduler load; the replacement's bounded promise allocation and microtask cost are negligible at the test's fixed cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. The change removes repeated timer work and does not increase request cardinality, retained lifetime, or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: ESLint analyzes mainThreadCustomEditors.test.ts with the timeout-polling rule after its exclusion is removed
Scenarios.CriticalPath: During lint, TypeScript parsing already occurs for the test file; the rule now receives loop-node callbacks and performs bounded AST checks for each loop. This work is on lint execution only and not any product startup, render, or interaction path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Loop-node count and shallow loop-body/ancestor size in one test file; effective cardinality is one newly included file per lint run.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: ESLint's existing file scheduling is unchanged. The rule adds no async work, worker, subprocess, queue, or external request; checks execute within the existing per-file traversal.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No rule-level cache is used or needed. The exclusion check and loop analysis are recomputed per lint invocation; removing one exclusion does not alter parser caching or cache keys.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the rule registers five loop visitors and checks only each loop body/ancestor chain. Repository inspection shows no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, network, or serialization boundary in the rule's changed applicability.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact lint overhead is unmeasured, but it is bounded by the small number of loop nodes in one already-parsed file and does not create an actionable scaling mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The incremental CPU work is small, bounded, and confined to lint, while enabling enforcement after the polling loops were removed.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all two changed files and every diff page. The PR replaces two unbounded timeout polling loops with one-shot DeferredPromise signals and removes the corresponding lint exclusion. The relevant repeated-work mechanism is reduced, promise lifetimes remain bounded by each test, and no product runtime or expensive external boundary is added. No valid performance finding or regression-fix learning record was supported.
